 5 weather alerts in effect North Dakota’s neighboring states raise their minimum wage 
 Minimum wage increases (KFYR-TV) By Sofia Morales Published : Nov. 18, 2026 at 11:25 AM CST | Updated : 4 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google BISMARCK, N.D. (KFYR) - South Dakota’s minimum wage is set to increase again in the new year.
 Their minimum wage for non-tipped employees will go up by 45 cents, going from $11.85 to $12.30.
 Montana is also raising their rates, from $10.85 to $11.20.
 Both take effect on Jan. 1, 2027. Both states experienced additional increases earlier this year. But here at home, rates haven’t moved for more than 17 years.
 North Dakota’s minimum wage remains at $7.25 an hour, the same rate workers have had since July of 2009.
